questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: When red blood cells are placed in distilled water, water enters them by osmosis until they swell and burst. The bursting of the red cells is called
questions.explanation: Fresh water swells the cell till its membrane gives way.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: After blood has clotted in a test tube, the pale yellow fluid that separates out on top, free of the clotting protein, is called
questions.explanation: It is plasma that has lost its fibrinogen.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A heavy smoker becomes breathless because the walls of his air sacs have broken down and fused into large weak sacs. This lung disease is
questions.explanation: The fine air sacs lose their elastic walls.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A disease in which the air passages of the lungs become narrow and produce much mucus, making breathing wheezy, is
questions.explanation: The tightened tubes whistle as air squeezes through.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A disease in which the body makes far too many abnormal white blood cells, crowding the marrow and weakening immunity, is
questions.explanation: The white cells multiply beyond all control.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A traveller sits still in a bus for many hours, and a clot forms inside the deep vein of his leg. A clot forming inside a blood vessel is called
questions.explanation: The clot grows where the blood flows too slowly.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A condition in which the blood pressure remains persistently higher than normal, straining the heart and the arteries, is
questions.explanation: The silent strain that doctors measure with a cuff.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The antibiotic obtained from the mould Penicillium, which kills bacteria by stopping their cell walls from forming, is
questions.explanation: Fleming's mould gave medicine its first antibiotic.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In the dry season, a mango tree forms a soft layer of cells at the base of each leaf stalk, and the leaves fall. The shedding that follows this layer is called
questions.explanation: The weak layer lets the leaf break cleanly away.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Inside a chloroplast, the green pigment sits in stacks of coin-like membranes. These stacks, the sites of the light reactions, are called
questions.explanation: Each chloroplast holds many of these stacks.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The fluid matrix of a chloroplast that surrounds the stacks of membranes, in which carbon dioxide is fixed into sugar, is the
questions.explanation: The sugar-building reactions run in this fluid.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: In photosynthesis, whichever requirement is in shortest supply — light, carbon dioxide or temperature — holds back the rate of the whole process. This is the law of
questions.explanation: The weakest link sets the pace of the chain.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: At dawn or dusk, the rate at which a leaf releases carbon dioxide by respiration exactly equals the rate at which it uses it in photosynthesis. This balance point is the
questions.explanation: At this moment the gas given out matches the gas taken in.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: Besides chlorophyll, leaves contain yellow and orange pigments that absorb light of other colours and pass the energy on to chlorophyll. These pigments are the
questions.explanation: Their colours show plainly in yellow maize and carrots.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A plant hormone that promotes cell division in roots and shoots and delays the ageing of leaves is
questions.explanation: Its name comes from cytokinesis, the dividing of cells.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The terminal bud of a young pine tree produces auxin that keeps the side buds below it from growing. This suppression of side branches by the growing tip is called
questions.explanation: Cut the tip and the sides are freed to sprout.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The system of naming every living thing with two Latin words, the first for its genus and the second for its species, is called
questions.explanation: Man is Homo sapiens under this two-name rule.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: An animal such as the earthworm, which carries both male and female reproductive organs in one body, is said to be
questions.explanation: One worm carries both bride and groom.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: People who carry one sickle-cell allele rarely suffer severe malaria, because the parasite finds their slightly altered red cells a poor home. This survival advantage of carriers is known as
questions.explanation: Carrying one allele shields them from the parasite.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The stage of life, roughly between ten and fourteen years, when a boy's or girl's reproductive organs mature and the secondary sexual characters appear, is called
questions.explanation: The body's clock first rings at this season.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A surgical method of family planning in which each sperm duct is cut and tied so that no sperm can leave the body is
questions.explanation: The duct that carries sperm is closed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A surgical method of family planning for women in which each fallopian tube is cut and tied so that no egg can reach the womb is
questions.explanation: The tubes that carry the eggs are sealed.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A thin rubber sheath worn over the male organ during mating, which stops sperm from reaching the egg, is a
questions.explanation: It is a barrier that the sperm cannot cross.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: A fruit such as the okra pod or the bean pod that splits open along one or more seams when ripe to release its seeds is described as
questions.explanation: Ripeness throws its doors open for the seeds.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.q: The red pigment found in muscle fibres, which stores a small supply of oxygen for the muscle to use during hard work, is
questions.explanation: It holds oxygen like a spare tank in the muscle.
